Market Overview & Transaction Summary

This analysis covers 5,000 Air Jordan secondary-market transactions spanning from 2023-01-01 to 2025-09-27. The average retail price across all transactions is $191.17, while the average resale price is $273.23, yielding an average profit margin of $82.06.

Of all transactions, 61.3% sold above retail — meaning 38.7% of transactions resulted in a loss relative to MSRP. The median profit margin is $35.27, indicating that the distribution is right-skewed with profitable outliers pulling up the mean. Average inventory holding time is 22.5 days (median: 14 days).

Impact of Shoe Condition on Resale Value

Condition is one of the strongest determinants of resale profitability. The data reveals a clear tiering:

Deadstock (Brand New) shoes command a resale premium of $323.38 (+244.7%) over Used shoes on average. VNDS shoes sit in between, trading at $97.71 (+73.9%) above Used.
  • Deadstock: Avg margin $264.01, premium rate 100.0%, avg resale $455.51
  • VNDS: Avg margin $37.62, premium rate 83.3%, avg resale $229.84
  • Used: Avg margin $-57.66, premium rate 0.0%, avg resale $132.13

Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations

Key Findings

  1. Condition is the primary profit driver. Deadstock shoes average $264.01 margin with a 100.0% premium rate, while Used shoes average $-57.66 — a swing of $321.67 per pair. VNDS occupies the middle ground at $37.62.
  2. Model and colorway selection matters significantly. Air Jordan 11 Retro leads with $99.84 average margin, while Air Jordan 1 Low lags at $50.52. The Pine Green colorway is the most profitable across all models.
  3. Channel choice involves a margin-velocity trade-off. Walk-in Retail yields the highest margins but may carry longer inventory holding periods. StockX offers the fastest turnover at 7.5 days, enabling capital recycling.
  4. The resale premium rate of 61.3% means roughly 39 in every 100 transactions sell below retail — careful sourcing and condition management are essential to profitability.

Strategic Recommendations

1. Prioritize Deadstock Sourcing. The condition premium is decisive. Focus acquisition on brand-new pairs — the probability of a profitable exit is dramatically higher. Avoid Used inventory unless acquisition cost is at least 58% below retail.
2. Focus on High-Margin Models and Colorways. Concentrate sourcing on Air Jordan 11 Retro and the Pine Green colorway. Use the model-colorway heatmap to identify high-margin combinations and avoid segments that consistently trade below retail.
3. Optimize Channel Mix Based on Strategy. For margin maximization, prioritize Walk-in Retail. For capital velocity and turnover, use StockX (avg 7.5 days). Consider a blended approach: list high-margin pairs on premium channels and move commodity inventory through faster platforms.
4. Time Your Buys and Sells Strategically. Monitor quarterly patterns to buy during lower-premium periods and sell into high-demand windows. Use the monthly trend data to identify seasonal momentum shifts.
5. Monitor Inventory Age. With an overall average of 22.5 days, pairs sitting beyond this threshold should be aggressively repriced or moved to faster channels to free capital.
